who: John Fraser Ramsey, historian of modern Europe at the University of Alabama, PhD Berkeley 1935.

evidence.says: John Fraser Ramsey received his PhD in modern European history at Berkeley in 1935 and taught at Alabama from 1935 until retirement in 1977, apart from wartime service.
Identifies John T. Ramsey as the University of Illinois at Chicago classicist, PhD Harvard 1975, and editor of Sallust.
Identifies James Gettys McGready Ramsey, the nineteenth-century Tennessee historian and physician, author of The Annals of Tennessee.

notes: Neither candidate is John Fraser Ramsey; the full names, academic careers and fields differ.

who: Andrew Wallace, historian of Arizona at Northern Arizona University.

evidence.says: A January 1971 review of Arizona Territory, 1863–1912 names Andrew Wallace and gives his affiliation as Northern Arizona University.
The candidate authority identifies the author of Virgil's Schoolboys (2010).
The author of Virgil's Schoolboys is a professor of English at Carleton, with MA and PhD degrees from Toronto and research in Renaissance literature and classical reception.

notes: The candidate is the Carleton literary scholar, whose doctorate and field differ from the Arizona-trained NAU supervisor.

who: George Winston Smith, historian at the University of New Mexico.

evidence.says: Barry A. Crouch's 1970 history dissertation, In Search of Union: Amos A. Lawrence and the Coming of the Civil War, lists George Winston Smith as committee chair.
Identifies George Gilbert Smith, a Civil War soldier and author of Leaves from a Soldier's Diary (1906), describing his service in 1861–1865.

notes: The named dissertation directly identifies the supervisor as George Winston Smith; the candidate is George Gilbert Smith, the Civil War diarist.

who: Goldwin Smith, historian at Wayne State University, PhD Cornell.

evidence.says: William Saffady's 1971 history PhD, Heresy and Popular Protestantism in England, 1527–1553, lists Goldwin Smith as first advisor.
A notice of the 1971 Franklin Lectures identifies Goldwin Smith as a Wayne State history professor with a Cornell PhD and author of A History of England.
The candidate held Oxford's Regius history professorship in 1858–1866 and taught at Cornell in 1868–1872; the item also carries LC n50013420.

notes: The Wayne State advisor and Cornell doctoral graduate is distinct from the nineteenth-century Oxford and Cornell professor.

who: Robert Harper Babcock, historian of Canadian-American labour at the University of Maine, PhD Duke 1970.

evidence.says: Identifies Robert Harper Babcock as Maine's emeritus history professor, with a Duke doctorate in 1970. He moved to Maine in 1975 and supervised doctoral dissertations there over the following two decades; his thesis became Gompers in Canada.
The authority for Robert H. (Robert Harper) Babcock identifies him as the author of Gompers in Canada (1974).
The other candidate, Robert Gary Babcock, completed his Duke doctoral thesis in 1983 and became a UNC Chapel Hill classics professor in 2008.

notes: Robert Harper Babcock matches both the Duke 1970 doctorate and the Maine supervision period. Robert Gary Babcock is a different scholar.

who: John F. Beeler, military and naval historian at the University of Alabama, PhD Illinois 1991.

evidence.says: Alabama lists John F. Beeler as professor, PhD Illinois 1991, researching military and naval history, Victorian Britain and imperial defence.
Identifies John Herbert Beeler, the UNC Greensboro scholar and author of Warfare in England, 1066–1189 and Warfare in Feudal Europe, 730–1200.
John Herbert Beeler studied medieval history at Cornell under Carl Stephenson and taught at UNC Greensboro throughout his career, 1950–1983.

notes: The candidate is John Herbert Beeler of UNC Greensboro, distinct from Alabama's Illinois-trained John F. Beeler.

who: Robert G. McPherson, historian of Britain and colonial Georgia at the University of Georgia.

evidence.says: The October 1960 article Georgia Slave Trials, 1837–1849 identifies Robert G. McPherson as assistant professor of history at the University of Georgia.

The publisher identifies Robert G. McPherson as a historian of colonial Georgia and the eighteenth- and nineteenth-century British Isles, author of Theory of Higher Education in Nineteenth-Century England (1959).
Identifies Robert Spowart McPherson of Utah State's Eastern-San Juan campus, a historian of Navajo and Ute history with a history PhD from Brigham Young University in 1987.

notes: The candidate's full name, BYU 1987 doctorate and Utah affiliation distinguish him from the Georgia supervisor with the supplied Johns Hopkins 1957 doctorate.

who: Richard Miles, history professor at Wayne State University.

evidence.says: The 1959–1960 Fulbright record identifies Richard Miles as associate professor of history at Wayne State University.
The candidate is the editor of Constructing Identities in Late Antiquity, a Cambridge-trained classicist later at Sydney, with a Liverpool BA and Cambridge PhD.
The candidate's item lists Cambridge and Liverpool education and employment at Cambridge, Trinity Hall and Sydney.

notes: The Wayne State supervisor with the supplied Michigan 1949 doctorate is distinct from the Cambridge-trained ancient historian represented by the candidate.
